canonical_statement: The review evaluated the effectiveness of further treatments for first and subsequent progression or recurrence of glioblastoma after standard Stupp-protocol primary therapy and prepared a brief economic commentary.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To evaluate the effectiveness of further treatment/s for first and subsequent progression or recurrence of glioblastoma (GBM) among people who have received the standard of care (Stupp protocol) for primary treatment of the disease; and to prepare a brief economic commentary on the available evidence.

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults aged 16 years or older with recurrent or progressive glioblastoma after primary surgery and chemoradiotherapy; mixed-primary-treatment studies were eligible when at least 80% received the standard 6-week Stupp protocol.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: People aged 16 years of age and older diagnosed with recurrent or progressive disease following primary treatment (surgery and chemoradiotherapy) for glioblastoma (GBM).

population.label: Adults with recurrent/progressive GBM after primary surgery and chemoradiotherapy
inclusion_criteria: Primary treatment included surgery and chemoradiotherapy; mixed cohorts required >=80% Stupp protocol

canonical_statement: Eligible effectiveness designs included randomized, quasi-randomized, non-randomized, and controlled before-and-after studies with concurrent comparison groups; uncontrolled, cross-over, case-control, dose-finding, and studies with fewer than 20 participants were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-randomised trials, non-randomised studies, and controlled before-and-after studies that included relevant concurrent comparison groups.

population.label: Eligible comparative effectiveness studies

canonical_statement: The review allowed any active chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, experimental treatment, or treatment combination compared with another active treatment, best supportive care, or no active treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Any active treatment (chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery or another experimental treatment) or treatment combination compared with another active treatment, best supportive (palliative) care or no active treatment.

exposures.details: Chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, experimental treatment, or combination

canonical_statement: Overall survival was defined as survival from study entry until death from all causes, or as reported by investigators.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Overall survival: survival from study entry until death from all causes, or as reported by investigators

outcome.definition: Survival from study entry until death from all causes, or as reported by investigators

canonical_statement: Health-related quality of life was a primary outcome measured with standardized instruments such as EORTC QLQ-C30/BN20 or FACT-G/FACT-Br.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Health-related quality of life (QoL): as measured using a standardised questionnaire, e.g. the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) QLQ-C30 or QLQ-BN20

outcome.definition: Standardized questionnaire such as EORTC QLQ-C30/BN20 or FACT-G/FACT-Br

canonical_statement: Progression-free survival was a secondary outcome defined as survival from study entry to disease relapse, or as defined by investigators.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Progression-free survival (survival from study entry to disease relapse, or as defined by investigators)

outcome.definition: Survival from study entry to disease relapse, or as defined by investigators

canonical_statement: Severe adverse events were defined as grade 3 or higher according to a standardized adverse-event measurement tool such as CTCAE.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Severe adverse events (grade 3 or higher according to a standardised measurement tool, such as the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE))

outcome.definition: Grade 3 or higher according to a standardized measurement tool such as CTCAE

canonical_statement: Effectiveness searches covered CENTRAL Issue 12 2019, MEDLINE from 2005 to December week 1 2019, and Embase from 2005 to 2019 week 50, with no language restrictions; trial registries, conference abstracts, and included-study reference lists were also searched.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For evidence on the effectiveness of interventions, we prepared the search strategies and conducted the searches of the following databases from January 2005 ... onwards

canonical_statement: At least two reviewers independently screened records and full texts; two reviewers independently extracted data using a piloted form, with disagreements resolved by discussion or consultation with other review authors.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A minimum of two reviewers (TL, ER, IL) independently screened the search results

canonical_statement: Randomized trials were assessed with the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool and non-randomized studies with ROBINS-I; risk-of-bias judgments were made independently by two review authors and incorporated into interpretation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For randomised trials, we assessed risk of bias using Cochrane's tool ... For non-randomised studies we used the ROBINS-I tool for assessing risk of bias.

canonical_statement: Time-to-event outcomes were summarized as hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals; dichotomous outcomes as risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals; continuous outcomes as mean differences with 95% confidence intervals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For time-to-event data (e.g. death or disease progression) we used the hazard ratio (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

canonical_statement: Pairwise meta-analyses used random-effects inverse-variance models, and network meta-analyses used random-effects multivariate models in Stata 15; separate networks were constructed for first recurrence and for mixed first/second/subsequent recurrence populations when connectivity and transitivity were judged adequate.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We used the random-effects model in Stata software (version 15) fitting a multivariate network meta-analysis

canonical_statement: The review used GRADE to assess certainty of evidence for overall survival, progression-free survival, and severe adverse events; quality-of-life data were insufficient for a Summary of Findings table.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There were insufficient data to present QoL findings. We used the GRADE system to rank the quality of the evidence.

canonical_statement: The review included 42 effectiveness studies: 34 randomized controlled trials and 8 non-randomized studies, involving 5,236 participants with progressive or recurrent glioblastoma.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We included 34 RCTs and 8 non-RCTs.

population.label: Participants across 42 included effectiveness studies with progressive/recurrent GBM

canonical_statement: The review judged randomized controlled trials generally at low or unclear risk of bias and non-randomized studies at high risk of bias; conference-abstract-only studies were generally unclear because of limited reporting.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In general, we judged RCTs to be at low or unclear risk of bias, and judged non-RCTs to be at high risk of bias.

canonical_statement: Publication bias could not be assessed with funnel plots because there were insufficient studies of similar interventions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We did not find sufficient studies of similar interventions to assess publication bias using funnel plots.

canonical_statement: Network meta-analysis could not be performed for second or subsequent recurrence because data were insufficient and the available studies did not form a sufficiently reliable connected network.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we could not perform NMAs of second and subsequent recurrence due to insufficient data.

canonical_statement: For second or later recurrence, evidence was sparse; limited heterogeneous studies suggested radiotherapy with or without bevacizumab might improve survival or progression outcomes in selected patients, but certainty was insufficient for firm conclusions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Limited evidence from three heterogeneous studies ... reported findings of improved PFS or OS with this intervention for all or for selected candidates. More evidence on radiotherapy with and without BEV is needed.

canonical_statement: Evidence from one RCT suggested little difference in progression-free or overall survival between tumour-treating fields and physician's choice of treatment in the second/later-recurrence context.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Evidence from one RCT suggested that there may be little difference in effects on PFS or OS of tumour-treating fields (TTF) compared with physician's choice of treatment in this context.

canonical_statement: The review found little good-quality evidence comparing treatment with best supportive care for second recurrence; the single bevacizumab-versus-supportive-care study was at high risk of bias.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We found little good-quality evidence that addressed this question as the one study that compared bevacizumab with best supportive care was at a high risk of bias.

canonical_statement: No randomized trials compared PCV with lomustine or evaluated temozolomide rechallenge as a standalone salvage strategy in the eligible post-Stupp population.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We found no RCTs comparing the commonly used regimen of PCV (procarbazine, lomustine and vincristine) and lomustine, or TMZ re-challenge.

canonical_statement: Most interventions other than lomustine and bevacizumab were supported by single, often open-label phase 2 studies with sparse data, reducing certainty and limiting phase-3-confirmed conclusions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Quality of evidence on other interventions was often from single studies and, therefore, tended to be of a lower quality due to the sparse data and open-label design of many of the phase 2 trials.

canonical_statement: For first recurrence after surgery and chemoradiotherapy, the review authors concluded that lomustine monotherapy appeared to be the best chemotherapy option among the evidence evaluated.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: lomustine (LOM) monotherapy appears to be the best chemotherapy option.

canonical_statement: The review authors concluded that adding bevacizumab to lomustine probably does not improve overall survival and increases the risk of severe adverse events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: adding bevacizumab to lomustine therapy probably does not improve overall survival and is associated with a significantly greater risk of severe adverse events.

canonical_statement: The review authors concluded that re-operation, with or without re-irradiation and chemotherapy, may be suitable for selected candidates with recurrent glioblastoma.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Re-operation with or without re-irradiation and chemotherapy may be suitable for selected candidates.

canonical_statement: For second recurrence, the review authors found little reliable evidence on re-irradiation with or without bevacizumab, best supportive care, or tumour-treating fields, leaving these roles uncertain.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We found little reliable evidence on re-irradiation with or without bevacizumab and on best supportive care. The role of tumour-treating fields is also uncertain.

canonical_statement: The review authors concluded that cost-effectiveness of treatment options for recurrent glioblastoma remained unclear because economic studies were lacking and methodologically inconsistent.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The cost-effectiveness of different treatment options for recurrent GBM remains unclear as economic studies in this field are lacking.
